newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Japan PM quits top opposition party.
newsitem.headline: Former Japan PM quits top opposition party.

text.p: Former Japanese prime minister Tsutomu Hata and 12 followers left the largest opposition party on Thursday to set up a new political group, ending months of squabbling in the party.
"This is a better step than continuously bickering within the party," Hata told reporters after the resignations.
Hata said his new party, called Taiyoto (Sun Party), would work with the party he had left, Shinshinto (New Frontier Party), to promote economic and administrative reforms.
"We share similar objectives to promote reform and I would like to maintain cooperative ties," Hata said.
Hata, 61, who helped found Shinshinto in 1994, has clashed with party leader and longtime political ally Ichiro Ozawa since the party made a poor showing in general elections in October.

The fractious Shinshinto was the product of the merger of nine political groups that formed the core of the reformist coalition governments that broke the Liberal Democratic Party's 38-year grip on power and ruled briefly in 1993 and 1994.
Shinshinto has spent much of its time and energy overcoming factionalism and has been unable to inspire voters or capitalise on unpopular government policies.

Hata, who like most members of both his old and his new parties started his career in the LDP, served as prime minister for two months before he was ousted in June 1994 and replaced by an LDP-dominated coalition.
